name: Combinatorial and Parent-Rank Laws for Partial Traces
statement: For nonempty $C\subseteq\{0,1\}^X$, with one mask coordinate $a_i$ for each $i\in X$, put $D(U)=\{i:i,a_i\in U\}$. Then $\operatorname{Sh}(T(C))=\{U:D(U)\in\operatorname{Sh}(C)\}$, the zero-mask section and full mask reduction both equal $C$, $\operatorname{VC}(T(C))=|X|+\operatorname{VC}(C)$, and $h(T(C))=h(C)+|X|$, including the value $+\infty$. A rank-$r$ parent with $m$ auxiliaries yields a rank-$(r+|X|)$ parent with at most $m+|X|$ auxiliaries while retaining the original mark.
proof: A trace on $U$ is realizable precisely when the old class can realize the coordinates whose value and mask are both prescribed with mask zero; this proves the shattering formula and VC shift. Membership is increasing in the masks, so the zero section equals the full reduction and is $C$. For one coordinate, the fiber theorem replaces the rank-one control fiber according to the unique old height and constructs a parent one rank higher with one new auxiliary. Iterate for the upper bound. Full reduction of any parent in all mask coordinates lowers rank by $|X|$ and leaves a parent of $C$, proving equality.
